doc.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Small bands, Harry James and joining Duke Ellington
title: First meeting Duke Ellington in Moline through Ben Webster
summary: Ellington's band played Moline, the hotel refused them, and Ben Webster introduced Bellson to Duke before they jammed all night.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Was that the first time you met Duke Ellington?

No. The first time I met Duke was in my hometown, Moline, Illinois, when Duke’s band came to town to play the Illinois Theater. That’s a good memory, right? I feel ashamed to say this, but Herb Jeffries was with the band, and they wouldn’t let the band stay at the hotel. They had to sleep on their bunks on the train. They came on the train. Duke offered to pay for the whole floor of the hotel. They still wouldn’t let him stay there. Herb Jeffries and I talk about that all the time. I met Duke then. I met Ben Webster first. I met him backstage. He said, “Come on. I want to introduce you to Duke.” I met Johnny Hodges, Duke, Ben Webster, Barney Bigard, Tricky Sam [Nanton], Lawrence Brown, all of them. Ben Webster told me, “Hey kid. You play drums, don’t you?” I say, “Yeah.” He said, “Where can I play, after the theater? I’d like to go out and do some jamming.” So him and I went out to Stan[?] Shores, a little place where they play jazz. I had a quartet. I played with Ben Webster all night long. I’ll never forget that. That’s an experience. We played so good. We wound up
just him and I. We left the trumpet player back – 10,000 choruses back. That’s how I met Duke – through Ben Webster.
Do you remember that meeting with Duke? Do you remember him.

Yeah. It was very congenial. He’s always been a trustworthy gentleman, always has time for you. I know he dug me because I didn’t ask him a lot of questions. I was brief. I could tell by the way he looked at me – let me check this dude out. He remembers that, later on – that meeting. He said, “I know, because Ben Webster told me, ‘You’ve got to hear this kid play’.” I think that was a break-in for me joining Duke’s band later on.
